盐跃层（共享「盐」这一成分的同族术语）

senses.title: Of heat and salt together
senses.definition: relating to temperature and salinity considered together as a pair of properties
senses.definitionCN: 把温度与盐度作为成对属性一并考虑的
senses.example: Every water sample has a thermohaline signature.
senses.exampleCN: 每个水样都带有温盐特征。
senses.why: Greek thermē 'heat' supplies the first half and halinos 'of salt' the second, with -ine joining them: the word names a pair, not a single quantity.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 thermē「热」提供前半，halinos「盐的」提供后半，再由 -ine 连接：这个词命名的是一对属性，而不是单一量值。

senses.title: Controlling density
senses.definition: describing the pair of properties that together fix the density of seawater
senses.definitionCN: 描述共同决定海水密度的两项属性
senses.example: Density is a thermohaline property of sea water.
senses.exampleCN: 密度是海水的一项温盐属性。
senses.why: cold water and salty water are both heavier, so heat and salt pull on the same lever; calling density thermohaline says which two dials control it.
senses.whyCN: 冷水和咸水都更重，热与盐拉的是同一根杠杆；把密度称为 thermohaline，就是说明哪两个旋钮在控制它。

senses.title: Driving the deep overturning
senses.definition: describing the temperature and salt differences that set the deep ocean circulation in motion
senses.definitionCN: 描述推动深层海洋环流运转的温度与盐度差异
senses.example: The deep flow is thermohaline in origin, not wind-driven.
senses.exampleCN: 这股深层流源于温盐作用，而不是风。
senses.why: wind moves the top of the sea, but sinking needs weight; only heat and salt can make water heavy enough to go down.
senses.whyCN: 风只动海面，下沉却需要重量；只有热与盐能让水重到可以往下走。

senses.title: Layering the water column
senses.definition: describing the layering of the water column that results from combined temperature and salinity differences
senses.definitionCN: 描述由温度与盐度差异共同造成的水柱分层
senses.example: A thermohaline boundary separates the two water masses.
senses.exampleCN: 一道温盐界面把两个水团分开。
senses.why: different heat and salt make water of different weight, and weight settles into layers instead of mixing away.
senses.whyCN: 不同的热与盐造出不同重量的水，而重量会沉淀成层，而不是混掉。

senses.title: Marking a water mass
senses.definition: describing the temperature and salinity values used to identify a particular body of water
senses.definitionCN: 描述用来辨认某一特定水体的温度与盐度数值
senses.example: Charting thermohaline properties lets a ship trace where a parcel came from.
senses.exampleCN: 测绘温盐性质能让船只追溯一块水来自何处。
senses.why: a water mass keeps the heat and salt it acquired at the surface, so the pair works as a label that travels with it.
senses.whyCN: 一个水团保留着它在表层获得的热与盐，因此这对数值成了随它旅行的标签。

senses.title: Forcing in a climate model
senses.titleCN: 气候模式中的温盐强迫
senses.definition: describing the surface fluxes of heat and fresh water that a climate model applies as thermohaline forcing
senses.definitionCN: 描述气候模式作为温盐强迫施加的热量与淡水通量
senses.example: The model applies thermohaline forcing at the high latitudes.
senses.exampleCN: 该模式在高纬地区施加温盐强迫。
senses.why: a model cannot move the ocean itself, so it must be given the heat and salt exchanges that will make water move.
senses.whyCN: 模式本身搬不动整个海洋，因此必须交给它那些会让水动起来的热量与盐分交换。

senses.title: The conveyor image
senses.definition: describing the slow global loop imagined as a conveyor belt driven by heat and salt
senses.definitionCN: 描述被想象成由热与盐驱动的全球缓慢环路
senses.example: The thermohaline conveyor is a shorthand for a loop no ship can follow in one lifetime.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐传送带是对一个没有船能在一生中走完的环路的简称。
senses.why: the loop is too slow and too large to see, so it is pictured as a belt: a mechanism, not a place.
senses.whyCN: 这个环路太慢太大，看不见，于是被画成一条传送带：一个机制，而不是一个地点。

senses.title: On a millennial clock
senses.definition: describing processes whose timescale runs to centuries or millennia rather than to seasons
senses.definitionCN: 描述时间尺度以百年或千年计而非以季节计的过程
senses.example: Thermohaline change is measured on a millennial clock.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐变化以千年的尺度来衡量。
senses.why: water that sinks must cross the whole basin before it rises, and that journey outlasts any human career.
senses.whyCN: 下沉的水要走完整个海盆才能重新上升，这段旅程比任何人的职业生涯都长。

senses.title: A signal in the sediment
senses.definition: describing ancient temperature and salinity conditions reconstructed from sediment or ice records
senses.definitionCN: 描述从沉积物或冰芯记录中重建的古代温度与盐度状况
senses.example: A thermohaline shift in the core matches the end of the cold period.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯中的温盐突变与寒冷期的结束相对应。
senses.why: shells and salts preserve the heat and salt of the water they formed in, so the pair becomes a readable trace of a vanished sea.
senses.whyCN: 贝壳与盐类保留着它们形成时水中的热与盐，于是这对数值成了对一片消失之海的可用痕迹。

intro.en: Thermohaline is a nineteenth-century scientific compound of two Greek stems: thermē 'heat' and hals 'salt' with its adjective halinos, joined by the English suffix -ine. It names water by the two properties that fix its density. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: thermohaline 是 19 世纪的科学复合词，由两个希腊词干构成：thermē「热」与 hals「盐」（及其形容词 halinos），再用英语后缀 -ine 连接；它以决定水密度的两项属性来命名水。年代均为约数。

items.en: Thermē 'heat' comes from thermos 'hot', the stem behind thermometer and thermic; it names the state, not the fire that produces it.
items.cn: thermē「热」来自 thermos「热的」，也是 thermometer 与 thermic 的词干；它命名状态，而不是产生热的火。

items.en: Hals, halos means 'salt' and also 'sea'; the adjective halinos 'of salt' is the form English borrowed for the second half of the compound.
items.cn: hals, halos 意为「盐」，也指「海」；形容词 halinos「盐的」就是英语借来构成复合词后半的形式。

items.en: The adjective ending -ine, from Latin -inus and French -ine, was the standard way nineteenth-century science turned a noun into a property adjective.
items.cn: 形容词词尾 -ine 来自拉丁 -inus 与法语 -ine，是 19 世纪科学把名词变成性质形容词的标准手段。

items.en: Physical oceanography needed a word for the pair of controls on density, and the Greek stems were joined rather than a phrase invented; the compound names what it measures.
items.cn: 物理海洋学需要一个词指控制密度的这对因素，于是把希腊词干拼接起来，而不是另造短语；这个复合词命名了它所测量的东西。

items.en: The compound became familiar through thermohaline circulation and the conveyor image, so the adjective now usually appears attached to circulation or stratification.
items.cn: 这个复合词通过温盐环流与传送带意象而为人熟知，因此如今这个形容词通常与 circulation 或 stratification 连用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and coiner, not the roots): the exact author and year of the first use are not established, and the PIE sources of both thermos and hals are reconstructions rather than attested forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指首见年代与造词者，不涉及词根）：最早用例的作者与年份没有定论；thermos 与 hals 的印欧来源均为重构形式，而非有文献可查的形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share one of the two Greek halves; group two holds words about salt, heat, density and layering that each cover only part of the idea.
note.cn: 第一组是共享两个希腊成分之一的词；第二组是关于盐、热、密度与分层的词，各自只覆盖这一概念的一部分。

entries.definition: relating to heat alone; it comes from the same Greek thermē but says nothing about salt.
entries.definitionCN: 只与热有关；同出希腊 thermē，却完全不涉及盐。

entries.definition: of or containing salt; it is the second half of thermohaline standing alone, with no heat in it.
entries.definitionCN: 盐的、含盐的；它是 thermohaline 的后半单独成词，其中没有热。

entries.definition: a layer of rapid temperature change in water; it shares therm- but names a boundary, not a pair of properties.
entries.definitionCN: 水中温度急剧变化的一层；共享 therm-，但命名的是一个界面，而不是一对属性。

entries.definition: a layer of rapid salinity change; it is the salt counterpart of the thermocline, and again a boundary rather than a property pair.
entries.definitionCN: 盐度急剧变化的一层；它是温跃层的盐度对应物，同样是一个界面而非一对属性。

entries.definition: containing salt; it measures one half of what thermohaline measures and ignores temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 含盐的；它只涉及 thermohaline 所量的一半，不涉及温度。

entries.definition: mass per unit volume; thermohaline properties are what make seawater density vary, so density is the outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 单位体积的质量；温盐性质是使海水密度变化的原因，因此密度是结果。

entries.definition: the arrangement of water in layers; thermohaline differences produce it, but the word itself says nothing about heat or salt.
entries.definitionCN: 水成层排列的状态；温盐差异造成这种排列，但这个词本身不涉及热或盐。

entries.definition: the upward force a fluid exerts; thermohaline contrasts create buoyancy differences, which is how they move water.
entries.definitionCN: 流体施加的向上之力；温盐差异造成浮力差，从而推动水运动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: therm- is heat: thermometer, thermal and thermocline all start here.
normal.cn: therm- 就是热：thermometer、thermal、thermocline 都从这里开始。

normal.en: hal- is salt: halite is rock salt, and haline means salty.
normal.cn: hal- 就是盐：halite 是岩盐，haline 意为含盐的。

normal.en: -ine is the adjective ending that turns a noun into a property, as in saline and marine.
normal.cn: -ine 是把名词变成性质形容词的词尾，如 saline 与 marine。

normal.en: The compound names its own cause: heat plus salt give density, and density drives the deep flow.
normal.cn: 这个复合词点明了自己的成因：热加盐给出密度，密度再驱动深层流。

normal.en: Its usual partners are fixed: thermohaline circulation, thermohaline stratification, thermohaline forcing.
normal.cn: 它的固定搭配很有限：温盐环流、温盐层化、温盐强迫。

abstract.en: Picture two dials on one bucket, one marked heat and one marked salt, both wired to the same scale.
abstract.cn: 想象桶上有两个旋钮，一个标热，一个标盐，都接到同一块刻度盘上。

abstract.en: Picture water that is too heavy to stay on top and has no choice but to sink.
abstract.cn: 想象水重得无法留在上层，除了下沉别无选择。

abstract.en: Picture a layer of water that refuses to mix with the layer beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一层水拒绝与它下面那层混合。

examples.en: Thermohaline differences make the deep water heavy enough to sink.
examples.cn: 温盐差异使深层水重到足以下沉。

examples.en: The basin's thermohaline structure changed after the ice melted.
examples.cn: 冰融化后，该海盆的温盐结构发生了改变。

examples.en: Models treat heat and fresh water as thermohaline forcing.
examples.cn: 模式把热量与淡水当作温盐强迫来处理。

dict_mnemonic.note: 拆词＋谐音记忆 · 非词源
dict_mnemonic.text: 「热么？海盐」——热与盐一起称量海水，决定它轻重 → 温盐的

root: 希腊 thermē「热」+ hals, halos「盐」的形容词 halinos「盐的」+ 英语后缀 -ine → thermohaline；19 世纪科学复合词，指温度与盐度共同作用；两个词根均属希腊语，无拉丁同族；thermē 与 hals 的更早印欧来源均为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one pair of dials: heat and salt named together, density fixed by them, sinking driven by density, layers formed, water masses labelled, model forcing supplied, the loop pictured as a belt, its slow clock, and its trace in old sediment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一对旋钮：热与盐并称、二者定下密度、密度驱动下沉、由此成层、给水团贴标签、给模式提供强迫、把环路画成传送带、它缓慢的时钟，以及它在古老沉积物中的痕迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two gauges in the same bucket, one reading heat and one reading salt, their two numbers deciding how heavy the water is.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一桶水里的两支量表，一支读热，一支读盐，两个读数决定这水有多重。

branches.en: THE TWO DIALS: heat and salt are named together because together they set density.
branches.cn: 两个旋钮：热与盐并称，因为二者合力定下密度。

branches.en: WHAT MAKES WATER MOVE: the same pair drives sinking in the sea and appears as forcing in a model.
branches.cn: 让水动起来的东西：同一对因素在海里驱动下沉，在模式里则表现为强迫。

branches.en: WHAT IT LEAVES BEHIND: layers in the column, and a signature that identifies a water mass.
branches.cn: 它留下的东西：水柱中的分层，以及辨认一个水团的标记。

branches.en: THE SLOW LOOP: pictured as a conveyor and measured on a millennial clock.
branches.cn: 缓慢的环路：被画成传送带，并以千年为尺度计量。

branches.en: A TRACE IN MUD: the pair survives in sediment as a record of an old sea.
branches.cn: 泥中的痕迹：这对数值在沉积物里留存，成为一片古海的记录。

intro.en: Thermohaline is a scientific compound made of two Greek roots and one English suffix; the same three pieces build the vocabulary of temperature and salt in water.
intro.cn: thermohaline 是由两个希腊词根加一个英语后缀构成的科学复合词；同样的三个构件搭建起水中温度与盐分的词汇。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative of this word: both roots are Greek, and only the suffix -ine reached English through Latin -inus and French -ine.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁同族：两个词根都是希腊语，只有后缀 -ine 是经拉丁 -inus 与法语 -ine 进入英语的。

senses.definition: ambitious and striving toward a goal or high position

senses.example: The studio is full of aspirant directors shooting short films.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室里挤满了拍摄短片的、雄心勃勃的准导演。

senses.example: Party aspirants competed for the nomination.
senses.exampleCN: 党内竞争者角逐提名。
senses.why: When the striving is personified, the adjective becomes the noun for the striver.
senses.whyCN: 当这种奋斗被拟人化，形容词就名词化为「奋斗者」。

intro.cn: aspirant 源自拉丁语 aspirare（向…呼气），由 ad-（朝向）加 spirare（呼吸）构成。

items.en: The root *speis- meant to blow or breathe.
items.cn: 词根 *speis- 意为吹、呼吸。

items.en: Spirare meant to breathe, giving spirit, inspire, respire.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为呼吸，派生 spirit、inspire、respire。

items.en: Aspirare meant to breathe on or toward, later to seek eagerly.
items.cn: aspirare 意为向…吹气，后引申为热切追求。

items.en: Aspirer kept the figurative pursuit sense.
items.cn: 古法语 aspirer 保留追求的比喻义。

items.en: English formed the noun aspirant for a seeker of high office.
items.cn: 十八至十九世纪英语由之构成名词 aspirant，指谋求高位者。

note.en: Aspirant names the person behind the verb aspire: the one still climbing.
note.cn: aspirant 是动词 aspire 背后的人：那个仍在攀登的人。

definition_zh: 问题解决；找出办法排除障碍、达到目标的过程或能力
definition_en: the process or skill of finding a way around an obstacle to reach a goal
core_image: 一团缠住的线被一根根理开，直到通路出现
scene: 水管突然漏水，父亲先关阀门，再逐段检查接头，最后换上新的密封圈。 The father shuts the valve, checks each joint in turn and finally fits a new seal, a calm exercise in problem-solving.

pos.zh: 问题解决的；用于解决问题的（作定语）

senses.title: The process of removing an obstacle
senses.definition: the sequence of steps by which an obstacle is identified and removed
senses.definitionCN: 识别并排除障碍的一连串步骤

senses.example: The class spent an hour on problem-solving with fractions.

senses.whyCN: 数学给了这个词最清晰的形式：明确的障碍、允许的步骤、可检验的终点。

senses.definition: designing or applying an algorithm that transforms an input into a required output
senses.definitionCN: 设计或应用把输入变成所需输出的算法
senses.example: The team improved problem-solving by splitting the task into subproblems.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把任务拆成子问题，从而改进了求解。
senses.why: a computer cannot improvise, so the process must be written as repeatable rules; that makes the phrase technical.
senses.whyCN: 计算机不能临场发挥，过程必须写成可重复的规则；这使该短语成为技术用语。

senses.title: Troubleshooting equipment
senses.definition: locating a fault in a machine or system and restoring it to work
senses.definitionCN: 找出机器或系统中的故障并使其恢复运作
senses.example: The technician's problem-solving began with the power supply.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员的问题解决从电源开始。
senses.why: engineering adds a physical object: the obstacle is a failed part, and the solution is a working machine.
senses.whyCN: 工程加上一个物理对象：障碍是坏掉的部件，方案是运转的机器。

senses.title: A research topic in cognitive psychology
senses.titleCN: 认知心理学的研究课题
senses.definition: the study of how people represent a goal, search a space of moves and choose a solution
senses.definitionCN: 研究人如何表征目标、搜索可能的步骤并选择方案
senses.example: Problem-solving is studied through puzzles and planning tasks.
senses.exampleCN: 问题解决通过谜题与计划任务来研究。
senses.why: psychologists ask what happens between reading a task and answering it, and the compound names that hidden interval.
senses.whyCN: 心理学家追问从读到题目到给出答案之间发生了什么，这个复合词命名那段看不见的间隔。

senses.title: Team and organizational solving
senses.titleCN: 团队与组织层面的问题解决
senses.definition: a group process for diagnosing a shared problem and agreeing on action
senses.definitionCN: 群体诊断共同问题并就行动达成一致的过程
senses.example: The staff used a weekly meeting for problem-solving across departments.
senses.exampleCN: 员工每周开会做跨部门的问题解决。
senses.why: when a problem belongs to no single person, the steps must be shared, and the phrase moves from a mind to a room.
senses.whyCN: 当问题不属于任何单个人时，步骤必须共享，这个短语便从一个脑袋移到一间屋子。

senses.title: Resolving conflict
senses.titleCN: 冲突调解与实际矛盾的处理
senses.definition: finding an arrangement that meets the interests of parties in dispute
senses.definitionCN: 找到兼顾争议各方利益的安排
senses.example: The mediator's problem-solving kept the two sides talking.
senses.exampleCN: 调解者的问题解决让双方继续谈下去。
senses.why: a conflict is an obstacle made of people, so the same steps apply: define the block, list options, test a solution.
senses.whyCN: 冲突是由人构成的障碍，因此同样适用：界定阻塞、列出选项、检验方案。

intro.en: Problem-solving joins Greek problēma 'a thing put forward' with Latin solvere 'to loosen'. The compound is modern English, though both halves are old. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: problem-solving 把希腊 problēma「被抛到前面之物」与拉丁 solvere「松开」连在一起。复合词是现代英语构造，两半都很古老。年代为约数。

items.en: Problem goes back to Greek proballein 'to throw forward', from pro- 'before' plus ballein 'to throw'; a problēma was a task or riddle put in front of someone.
items.cn: problem 可追溯到希腊 proballein「向前抛出」，由 pro-「在前」加 ballein「投掷」构成；problēma 就是摆在人面前的题目或谜语。

items.en: The noun problēma meant 'a thing put forward, a task, a question for debate'; Latin borrowed it as problema.
items.cn: 名词 problēma 意为「被提出之物、任务、待辩的问题」；拉丁语借作 problema。

items.en: Solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve, pay'; the metaphor of untying a knot is what solving a problem still carries.
items.cn: solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解、偿付」；「解开一个结」的比喻至今仍留在「解决问题」这一说法中。

items.en: Problem entered English in the sixteenth century through French; problem-solving as a fixed compound is recorded only in modern usage, especially after psychology and computing adopted it.
items.cn: problem 经法语在 16 世纪进入英语；problem-solving 作为固定复合词只见于现代用法，尤其在心理学与计算领域采用之后。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the first use of the hyphenated compound is not precisely recorded, and Greek ballein has no reliable Latin cognate, so the Latin list covers only the solving half.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：带连字符的复合词最早用法没有精确记录；希腊 ballein 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条只覆盖「解决」这一半。

note.en: Group one holds forms and spellings that are easily confused; group two holds related activities that are not identical with solving a problem.
note.cn: 第一组是易混的形式与拼写；第二组是相关但并不等同于「解决问题」的活动。

entries.definition: The same compound written as two words; the unhyphenated form is common when it is used as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个复合词写成两个词；作名词时无连字符形式很常见。

entries.definition: A person who solves problems; the agent noun adds -er, while problem-solving names the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 解决问题的人；施动名词加 -er，而 problem-solving 命名活动。

entries.definition: The difficulty itself, before any solution; solving is the response to it.
entries.definitionCN: 困难本身，尚未有方案；solving 是对它的回应。

entries.definition: The answer or arrangement that removes the difficulty; problem-solving is the road, solution the destination.
entries.definitionCN: 消除困难的答案或安排；problem-solving 是路，solution 是终点。

entries.definition: Locating and fixing faults in equipment; it is the engineering branch of problem-solving.
entries.definitionCN: 找出并修复设备故障；是问题解决在工程中的分支。

entries.definition: Selecting among options; solving a problem usually includes a decision, but the two are not the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 在选项中选择；解决问题通常包含决策，但两者不是同一动作。

entries.definition: Moving from premises to conclusions; it is one tool used inside problem-solving.
entries.definitionCN: 从前提走向结论；是问题解决中使用的一种工具。

entries.definition: Settling a dispute between parties; it applies problem-solving to social conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 解决各方争议；把问题解决用于社会冲突。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: pro- 'before' + ballein 'throw' gives a thing thrown in your path; solvere 'untie' gives the act of clearing it.
normal.cn: pro-「在前」+ ballein「投掷」= 扔到你路上的东西；solvere「解开」= 清走它的动作。

normal.en: The family runs problem, solve, solution, solvable and problem-solver.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 problem、solve、solution、solvable 与 problem-solver。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: problem-solving skills, the problem-solving process, collaborative problem-solving.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：问题解决技能、问题解决过程、协作式问题解决。

normal.en: Mathematics and computing give the phrase its strictest form: stated input, allowed steps, checkable output.
normal.cn: 数学与计算给出这个短语最严格的形式：明确输入、允许步骤、可检验输出。

normal.en: A problem is the obstacle; a solution is the cleared path.
normal.cn: problem 是障碍，solution 是清出来的路。

abstract.en: Picture a knot in a rope, then a finger working one loop loose at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象绳上有个结，一根手指一圈圈把它挑松。

abstract.en: Picture a blocked pipe and a hand tracing the blockage joint by joint.
abstract.cn: 想象堵塞的管道，一只手一段段地摸到堵点。

abstract.en: Picture a maze where every wrong turn is marked before the right one is found.
abstract.cn: 想象一座迷宫，每个错弯都被标出之后才找到对的那条。

examples.en: The course teaches problem-solving through real case studies.
examples.cn: 这门课通过真实案例教授问题解决。

examples.en: Good problem-solving begins with a clear statement of the goal.
examples.cn: 好的问题解决始于对目标的清晰陈述。

examples.en: The team's collaborative problem-solving shortened the repair by days.
examples.cn: 团队的协作式问题解决把维修缩短了好几天。

dict_mnemonic.text: problem（难题）+ solving（解决）——把挡路的难题解开 → 问题解决

root: problem 源自希腊 problēma「被抛出之物」← proballein（pro- 在前 + ballein 投掷）；solving 源自拉丁 solvere「解开」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the clearing of a path: the steps, the skill, the mathematics, the algorithm, the broken machine, the hidden mental search, the shared room, and the conflict between people.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「清出一条路」展开：步骤、技能、数学、算法、坏掉的机器、看不见的心智搜索、共享的会议室，以及人与人之间的冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a knot loosened loop by loop until the rope runs free.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个结被一圈圈挑松，直到绳子重新通畅。

branches.en: THE LOOP: goal, barrier, analysis, plan, trial and resolution is the minimal complete shape.
branches.cn: 循环：目标、障碍、分析、计划、尝试与解决构成最小的完整形状。

branches.en: CAPACITY: a loop repeated well becomes a skill that tests can measure.
branches.cn: 能力：循环做得好，就成为测验可测量的技能。

branches.en: FORMAL MODELS: mathematics and algorithms make the steps explicit and checkable.
branches.cn: 形式模型：数学与算法让步骤明确且可检验。

branches.en: THE BROKEN OBJECT: engineering turns the obstacle into a faulty part.
branches.cn: 坏掉的物件：工程把障碍变成一个坏部件。

branches.en: MIND, ROOM, RELATION: the same loop runs silently in a head, openly in a team, and between opposing sides.
branches.cn: 心智、房间、关系：同一条循环在脑中无声进行，在团队中公开进行，也在对立双方之间进行。

intro.en: Problem-solving is a compound of two borrowings: a Greek noun of obstruction and a Latin verb of loosening, joined by the English -ing form.
intro.cn: problem-solving 是两个借词的复合：一个希腊的「阻塞」名词与一个拉丁的「松开」动词，由英语 -ing 形式连接。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere 'to loosen' supplies solve, solution, solvable and solvent; Greek problēma supplies problem. The two halves come from different languages and must not be forced into one root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 solvere「松开」提供 solve、solution、solvable 与 solvent；希腊 problēma 提供 problem。两半来自不同语言，不能强行并成一个词根。

items.example: Pro- places the task in front of the solver.
items.exampleCN: pro- 把任务摆在解题者面前。

items.example: Ballein also appears in ballistic.
items.exampleCN: ballein 也出现在 ballistic 中。

items.meaning: a thing put forward, a task
items.example: Problēma entered Latin as problema.
items.exampleCN: problēma 以 problema 进入拉丁语。

items.example: Solvere is the source of solve and solution.
items.exampleCN: solvere 是 solve 与 solution 的来源。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb solve into the activity of solving.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词 solve 变成「解决」这项活动。

items.meaning: a difficulty to be dealt with
items.example: The problem was a cracked joint.
items.exampleCN: 问题是一个裂开的接头。

items.example: She solved the puzzle in a minute.
items.exampleCN: 她一分钟就解开了谜题。

items.meaning: the act or result of loosening
items.example: The solution was a new seal.
items.exampleCN: 解决办法是换一个新密封圈。

items.example: Not every dispute is solvable at once.
items.exampleCN: 并非每场争议都能立刻解决。

items.meaning: a person skilled at finding solutions
items.example: A good problem-solver asks what the real goal is.
items.exampleCN: 善于解决问题的人会先问真正的目标是什么。

definition_zh: （使）断裂；裂缝；骨折；岩体破裂；分裂
definition_en: to break or crack a hard solid, or the break itself, especially in bone or rock
core_image: 一块完好的石板被凿子沿着一条细线敲开，断面新鲜而锋利
scene: 地质实验室里，学生把岩芯夹在台钳上，准备沿薄弱面敲开。 A geologist uses a chisel to fracture the core sample and expose a fresh surface.
sceneCN: 这里 fracture 是动词「使断裂、敲裂」（第 1 个义项：把坚硬固体沿薄弱面破开）；句意为地质学家用凿子敲裂岩芯样品，露出新鲜断面。

pos.zh: 使断裂；敲裂；使骨折；使分裂
裂缝；断裂；骨折；岩体破裂

collocations.zh: 发丝般细的裂缝；细微骨折

derivatives.zh: 断裂的；分裂的；支离破碎的
分数；小部分（同出 frangere，但语义已分流）
碎片；片段（同出 frangere 的另一支）
易碎的；脆弱的（同出 frangere）
使折射（re- 加 frangere，指光线折断）

senses.title: Break a hard solid on purpose
senses.definition: to break or crack a hard material such as rock, metal or glass
senses.definitionCN: 使岩石、金属、玻璃等坚硬材料破裂或出现裂缝
senses.example: A geologist uses a chisel to fracture the core sample.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家用凿子敲裂岩芯样品。
senses.why: fracture comes from Latin fractura, a breaking, from frangere, to break; the verb is the act that produces a fractura.
senses.whyCN: fracture 来自拉丁 fractura「断裂」，源自动词 frangere「打破」；动词义就是产生一道断裂的动作。

senses.title: The crack that results
senses.definition: a crack or line of breakage in a solid object
senses.definitionCN: 固体物件上出现的裂缝或断线
senses.example: A hairline fracture ran across the marble slab.
senses.exampleCN: 一条发丝般的细裂缝横过大理石板。
senses.why: Latin fractura named both the act and its result, and English kept the same double life in one noun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fractura 同时指动作与结果，英语把这个双重身份原样保留在同一个名词里。

senses.title: Break a bone
senses.definition: to crack or break a bone in the body
senses.definitionCN: 使身体中的骨头裂开或折断
senses.example: He fractured his wrist when he fell off the ladder.
senses.exampleCN: 他从梯子上摔下来，手腕骨折了。
senses.why: a bone is the hardest solid in the body, so the general sense of breaking a hard thing settled naturally on bone.
senses.whyCN: 骨头是身体里最硬的固体，因此「敲断硬物」的一般义自然落在骨折上。

senses.title: A break in the rock mass
senses.definition: a planar break through rock along which the two sides have moved or can move
senses.definitionCN: 贯穿岩层、两侧已发生或可能发生位移的破裂面
senses.example: The fault is a fracture that has slipped many times.
senses.exampleCN: 这条断层是一条多次滑动的破裂面。
senses.why: geology took the everyday noun and made it precise: a fracture is any break, a fault is one that has actually slipped.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把日常名词精确化：fracture 泛指破裂，fault 专指真正发生过滑动的那一条。

senses.title: Split a group into camps
senses.titleCN: 使团体分裂成对立阵营
senses.definition: to divide a group, party or alliance into opposing parts
senses.definitionCN: 使团体、政党或联盟分裂为对立的几部分
senses.example: The dispute fractured the alliance into three camps.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争端把联盟分裂成三个阵营。
senses.why: the image of a solid breaking into pieces was transferred from stone to social bodies, which also lose their wholeness.
senses.whyCN: 固体碎成数块的意象被移用到社会群体上，因为群体同样会失去完整。

senses.title: A split in unity or agreement
senses.definition: a division or breach in something previously united, such as trust or consensus
senses.definitionCN: 原本统一之物（如信任或共识）出现的分裂或缺口
senses.example: The report exposed a fracture in the coalition's common position.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告暴露出联盟共同立场上的一道裂口。
senses.why: the noun sense extends the physical crack to anything that can no longer be described as one piece.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把物理裂缝扩展到一切不再能被称作「一整块」的事物。

senses.title: The way a mineral breaks
senses.definition: the characteristic surface shape a mineral shows when it breaks other than along cleavage planes
senses.definitionCN: 矿物不沿解理面断开时所呈现的特征断面形态
senses.example: Quartz shows a conchoidal fracture rather than flat cleavage.
senses.exampleCN: 石英呈现贝壳状断口，而不是平整的解理面。
senses.why: mineralogy needed a word for the surface left by breaking, and fracture already meant exactly that result.
senses.whyCN: 矿物学需要一个词指断裂留下的表面，而 fracture 本来就表示这个结果。

senses.title: Break the continuity of something abstract
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：打断某种连续性
senses.definition: to break the continuity or smooth working of a system, narrative or relationship
senses.definitionCN: 打断系统、叙事或关系的连续性或顺畅运转
senses.example: One missing shipment can fracture a delicate supply chain.
senses.exampleCN: 一次缺货就可能打断一条脆弱的供应链。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the core gesture: something that was continuous is now interrupted by a break.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留核心动作：原本连续的东西，如今被一道断口打断。

intro.en: Fracture comes from Latin fractura, a breaking, from the verb frangere, to break, whose past participle is fractus. The word entered English in the fifteenth century, first as the medical name for a broken bone.
intro.cn: fracture 来自拉丁 fractura「断裂」，出自动词 frangere「打破」，其过去分词为 fractus。该词于 15 世纪进入英语，最初是骨折的医学名称。

items.en: Frangere meant to break, shatter or smash. Its past participle fractus supplied the stem frac- seen in fracture, fraction and fragment.
items.cn: frangere 意为「打破、击碎、砸碎」。其过去分词 fractus 提供了 fracture、fraction、fragment 中所见的 frac- 词干。

items.en: Fractura was the noun of result, a breaking or the breach produced by it, used for broken bones as well as broken objects.
items.cn: fractura 是结果名词，指「断裂」或断裂造成的破口，既用于断骨，也用于破碎的物件。

items.en: English took fracture in the fifteenth century as a term for a broken bone, alongside the older verb break.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪借入 fracture，作为骨折的术语，与更古老的动词 break 并存。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word was applied to rock masses and to manufactured materials, where a fracture is a plane of breakage.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，该词被用于岩体与人工材料，其中 fracture 指一个破裂面。

items.en: In modern usage a society, party or narrative can be fractured, extending the stone image to anything that loses its wholeness.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，社会、政党或叙事都可以被 fracture，把石头的意象扩展到一切失去完整性的东西。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the link of frangere to a reconstructed Indo-European root for breaking is a standard reconstruction, not a recorded form; the first date of the geological sense is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：frangere 与重构的印欧语「打破」词根之间的联系属于标准重构，并非有记录的形式；地质义的首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin breaking stock; group two holds near neighbours that also describe damage or division.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「打破」词干的词；第二组是同样表示损坏或分裂的近义词。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective: cracked, split or disjointed, as in a fractured skull or a fractured story.
entries.definitionCN: 本词的过去分词作形容词：裂开的、分裂的、支离破碎的，如骨折的头骨或破碎的叙事。

entries.definition: From the same frangere stock: a piece broken off something larger, so it names the result rather than the break.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 frangere：从更大物体上掉下的一块，指结果而非断裂本身。

entries.definition: Also from fractus, but it shifted to a numerical part of a whole and no longer means a physical break.
entries.definitionCN: 同样来自 fractus，但语义转向「整体的数值部分」，不再指物理断裂。

entries.definition: From frangere through French: easily broken, describing a quality rather than an event.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自 frangere：容易破碎的，描述性质而非事件。

entries.definition: A narrow line of breakage or a sharp splitting sound; it can be smaller than a fracture and need not separate the parts.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄的裂线或清脆的爆裂声；可以比 fracture 更轻，且两半不必分离。

entries.definition: The general English verb for separating into pieces; fracture is its technical and medical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 表示分成数块的一般英语动词；fracture 是它技术化、医学化的对应词。

entries.definition: To divide along a line, often cleanly, as wood splits; it stresses separation rather than shattering.
entries.definitionCN: 沿一条线分开，常指干脆地劈开，如木头裂开；强调分离而非碎成多块。

entries.definition: A sudden tearing or bursting of something under pressure, such as a pipe or a tendon; it adds force to the idea of breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 受压之物突然撕裂或爆开，如管道或肌腱；在「断裂」之上加了「受力爆裂」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: frac- is the broken stem: frangere broke things, and fractus is the broken result.
normal.cn: frac- 就是「断」的词干：frangere 打破东西，fractus 是打破的结果。

normal.en: The family runs fracture, fractured, fracturing, fraction, fragment, fragile and refract.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fracture、fractured、fracturing、fraction、fragment、fragile、refract。

normal.en: Medical phrases fix the bone sense: hairline fracture, stress fracture, compound fracture.
normal.cn: 医学搭配固定了骨折义：细微骨折、应力性骨折、开放性骨折。

normal.en: Geology pairs it with fault and fracture zone, where the break is a plane in rock.
normal.cn: 地质学把它与断层、断裂带配对，此时断口是岩体中的一个面。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object: fracture a bone, fracture a rock, fracture an alliance.
normal.cn: 动词直接带宾语：使骨折、敲裂岩石、使联盟分裂。

abstract.en: Picture a plate that looks whole until a hairline runs across it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只看似完好的盘子，直到一条细线横穿而过。

abstract.en: Picture a team photo with one person cut out of the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一张团队合影，其中一个人被从画面里裁掉。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that stops in the middle because the thought itself broke.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话说到一半就停住，因为那个念头本身断了。

examples.en: The impact fractured the limestone into angular blocks.
examples.cn: 撞击把石灰岩碎成有棱角的岩块。

examples.en: She fractured her ankle while stepping off the curb.
examples.cn: 她在下路缘时扭断了脚踝。

examples.en: The vote fractured the party along regional lines.
examples.cn: 这次投票使该党沿地域界线分裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fract（断）+ ure」——像石头被敲出一道缝 → 断裂、骨折、分裂

root: 拉丁 frangere「打破」的过去分词 fractus + 名词后缀 -ura → fractura「断裂」；英语 fracture。同族含 fraction、fragment、fragile、refract。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one event: a hard thing loses its wholeness. The event is then named as a noun, located in bone, made a plane in rock, and finally applied to groups, agreements, mineral surfaces and systems.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个事件展开：坚硬之物失去完整。这个事件先被名词化，再落到骨头、岩体中的平面，最后用于群体、共识、矿物断面与系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sound slab that acquires a sharp new line and is no longer one piece.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块完好的石板出现一道锋利的新线，从此不再是一整块。

branches.en: ACT AND RESULT: the verb names the blow, the noun names the line it leaves.
branches.cn: 动作与结果：动词指那一下敲击，名词指它留下的那条线。

branches.en: BONE: the body's hardest solid is the most personal place a fracture can happen.
branches.cn: 骨头：身体里最硬的固体，是断裂最能切身发生的地方。

branches.en: ROCK AND MINERAL: geology turns the break into a measurable plane or surface.
branches.cn: 岩石与矿物：地质学把断裂变成可测量的平面或断面。

branches.en: SOCIAL SPLIT: a group, like a slab, can lose its wholeness along a line.
branches.cn: 社会分裂：群体和石板一样，会沿一条线失去完整。

branches.en: SYSTEM BREAK: continuity itself is what snaps in the abstract use.
branches.cn: 系统中断：抽象用法里断掉的是连续性本身。

intro.en: Fracture is a Latin noun of result built from a verbal stem plus a suffix, and the same stem recurs across English.
intro.cn: fracture 是由动词词干加后缀构成的拉丁结果名词，同一词干在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin frangere, fractus and fractura give fracture, fraction, fragment, fragile, refract and frangible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 frangere、fractus 与 fractura 衍生 fracture、fraction、fragment、fragile、refract 与 frangible。

items.example: The stem frac- carries the result of breaking.
items.exampleCN: 词干 frac- 承载「打破之后的结果」。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: Fractura is the result noun built on the participle.
items.exampleCN: fractura 是在分词之上构成的结果名词。

items.example: The chisel fracture left a clean edge.
items.exampleCN: 凿出的断裂留下干净的边。

items.meaningCN: 断裂的；分裂的；支离破碎的
items.example: The fractured rock face showed several sets of joints.
items.exampleCN: 断裂的岩面显出好几组节理。

items.example: Hydraulic fracturing opened the shale.
items.exampleCN: 水力压裂打开了页岩。

items.meaning: a breaking into parts, hence a numerical part
items.meaningCN: 分成部分，后指数值上的分数
items.example: Only a fraction of the sample survived.
items.exampleCN: 样品中只有一小部分留存。

items.example: Fragments of the core lay on the bench.
items.exampleCN: 岩芯的碎片散在实验台上。

items.example: The fragile shell cracked at a touch.
items.exampleCN: 脆薄的壳一碰就裂。

items.meaning: to bend a ray back as it passes
items.example: Water refracts the light entering it.
items.exampleCN: 水使进入其中的光发生折射。

items.example: The frangible target shattered on impact.
items.exampleCN: 易碎靶一受撞击就碎。

definition_zh: 算法；解题步骤；计算方法
definition_en: a finite step-by-step procedure for solving a problem or carrying out a computation
core_image: 一张纸上画着一串带箭头的方框，每一步都指向下一步，最后停在一个写有结果的圆里
scene: 纸上画着一串带箭头的方框，每一步都指向下一步，最后停在一个写有结果的圆里。 The nurse followed the sorting algorithm step by step until every record was in order.
sceneCN: 这里 algorithm 指为解决某个问题而规定的一串有限步骤（第 1 个义项：解决问题的有限步骤序列）；句意：护士按这套排序算法一步步执行，直到每份记录都归了位。图中可辨识物件：方框、箭头、末端圆框、结果字样。

pos.zh: 算法；解题步骤；计算方法

derivatives.zh: 阿拉伯数字记数法；十进制算法

senses.title: A finite procedure for a problem
senses.definition: a set of steps that always ends and always yields an answer for the allowed inputs
senses.definitionCN: 对允许的输入总能终止并给出答案的一组步骤
senses.example: The manual gives an algorithm for checking every receipt twice.
senses.exampleCN: 手册给出了一套把每张收据核对两遍的算法。
senses.why: the word began as the name of a written calculating method, so its core sense is a method laid out step by step rather than a single trick.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指一种写下来的计算方法，核心义因此是按步骤铺开的方法，而不是某个单点窍门。

senses.title: A procedure precise enough for a computer
senses.titleCN: 精确到可交给计算机执行的步骤
senses.definition: a procedure stated so exactly that a machine can carry it out without guessing
senses.definitionCN: 表述得足够精确，机器无需猜测即可执行的步骤
senses.example: The algorithm must say what to do at every branch, not just at the start.
senses.exampleCN: 算法必须说明每个分支该做什么，而不只是开头怎么做。
senses.why: computers removed every human gap in the procedure, so the modern sense stresses total explicitness.
senses.whyCN: 计算机抹掉了步骤中一切由人填补的空隙，现代词义因此强调完全的明确性。

senses.title: The method as an object of study
senses.definition: the abstract object whose running time and memory use can be measured and compared
senses.definitionCN: 可以测量并比较运行时间与内存占用的抽象对象
senses.example: Two algorithm designs can give the same answers at very different costs.
senses.exampleCN: 两种算法设计可以给出相同答案，代价却差得很远。
senses.why: once procedures were written formally, they could be analysed like mathematical objects, and the noun named that object.
senses.whyCN: 步骤一旦被形式化地写出，就能像数学对象一样被分析，名词便指这个对象。

senses.title: A named routine in software
senses.definition: a standard procedure such as sorting or searching, often named after its strategy
senses.definitionCN: 排序、搜索等标准步骤，常按其所用策略命名
senses.example: The sort algorithm merges small lists before joining them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个排序算法先把小列表合并，再把它们接起来。
senses.why: libraries of reusable procedures needed names, and each named procedure was called an algorithm after its method.
senses.whyCN: 可复用的过程库需要名字，每个具名过程依其方法被称为一个算法。

senses.title: A rule set for calculation
senses.definition: a fixed set of rules for performing arithmetic with written numerals
senses.definitionCN: 用写出的数字进行算术运算的固定规则集
senses.example: The medieval algorithm for long division spread with Arabic numerals.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的长除法算法随阿拉伯数字一起传播。
senses.why: the oldest sense is simply the rules of decimal calculation that the word's namesake taught, and this sense survives in the older spelling algorism.
senses.whyCN: 最老的意思就是这个词的同名者所教的十进制计算规则，这一义保存在较早拼写 algorism 里。

senses.title: A decision procedure in logic
senses.definition: a mechanical method that decides, in finitely many steps, whether a statement follows from given rules
senses.definitionCN: 在有限步内判定某陈述是否可由给定规则推出的机械方法
senses.example: No algorithm decides every question in that formal system.
senses.exampleCN: 没有算法能判定该形式系统里的每一个问题。
senses.why: logic borrowed the word for any mechanical decision method, because such a method removes the need for insight at each step.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借这个词指任何机械判定方法，因为这类方法免去了每一步都要靠洞察。

senses.title: The rule set inside a service
senses.titleCN: 服务内部运行的规则集
senses.definition: the scoring or ranking rules that decide what a platform shows to a user
senses.definitionCN: 决定平台向用户展示什么的评分或排序规则
senses.example: The feed algorithm ranks posts by how long people linger.
senses.exampleCN: 信息流算法按人们停留的时间给帖子排序。
senses.why: platforms turned a formal procedure into a product feature, and users met the word as the invisible rule behind what they see.
senses.whyCN: 平台把形式化步骤变成产品功能，用户于是把这个词理解为眼前内容背后那条看不见的规则。

senses.title: A procedure for routing or scheduling
senses.definition: the rule set a network or system uses to choose paths, times or resources
senses.definitionCN: 网络或系统用来选择路径、时间或资源的规则集
senses.example: The routing algorithm sends each packet along the least crowded link.
senses.exampleCN: 路由算法让每个数据包走最不拥挤的链路。
senses.why: networks must choose among options thousands of times a second, and any such choice rule is naturally called an algorithm.
senses.whyCN: 网络每秒要在众多选项中做出成千上万次选择，这类选择规则自然就叫算法。

senses.title: A recipe for doing something
senses.definition: a fixed, often unthinking way of proceeding in everyday matters
senses.definitionCN: 日常事务中固定、常常无需思考的处理方式
senses.example: There is no algorithm for choosing whom to trust.
senses.exampleCN: 挑选该信任谁，并没有现成的算法。
senses.why: when people say there is no algorithm for something, they mean no reliable step-by-step rule exists, which is the word used in its broadest everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 当人们说某事没有算法时，意思是并不存在可靠的逐步规则，这是这个词最宽泛的日常用法。

intro.en: Algorithm is an eponym: it comes from the Latinised name of the ninth-century mathematician al-Khwarizmi, whose textbook taught decimal calculation. The -th- spelling is a later mistake, not part of the name. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algorithm 是一个由人名转来的词：出自九世纪数学家花拉子米的拉丁化名字，他的教科书传授十进制计算。词中的 -th- 是后来的误写，并非名字的一部分。年代均为约数。

items.en: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi worked in Baghdad in the ninth century and wrote a treatise on calculation with Indian numerals.
items.cn: 穆罕默德·伊本·穆萨·花拉子米在九世纪的巴格达工作，写有一部讲述用印度数字计算的论著。

items.en: Translators Latinised his name as Algoritmi, which became the label for his calculation method rather than for the man.
items.cn: 译者把他的名字拉丁化为 Algoritmi，这个词后来成了他所教计算法的标签，而不再指这个人。

items.en: Medieval Latin algorismus named the decimal system and the rules for using it, and English algorism came from that form.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 指十进制及其使用规则，英语 algorism 即由这一形式而来。

items.en: Writers linked the unfamiliar word to Greek arithmos, number, and altered the spelling to algorithm; the false link is documented and was never corrected.
items.cn: 写作者把这个陌生词与希腊语 arithmos「数」联系起来，把拼写改成 algorithm；这一错误联系有记录，且从未被纠正。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word shifted from written arithmetic rules to any precise procedure that a machine can execute.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词从书面的算术规则转为指任何机器可以执行的精确步骤。

items.en: Generally accepted: the personal name refers to Khwarazm, a region south of the Aral Sea, which older sources spell in more than one way. The derivation of the word from his name is documented; only the ancient spellings of the place vary.
items.cn: 一般认为是：这个人名指咸海南面的花拉子模地区，古代文献对该地名有不止一种拼写。这个词由他的名字转来有文献依据，可变的只是地名的古代拼写。

note.en: The first group shares the name or the spelling and is easily confused; the second group names neighbouring ideas of method, rule and shortcut.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一人名来源或形近，容易混淆；第二组是与方法、规则、捷径相邻的概念。

entries.definition: The older English word for the decimal system and its calculation rules; algorithm is the later, respelled descendant.
entries.definitionCN: 指十进制及其计算规则的较早英语词；algorithm 是后来改拼的变体。

entries.definition: Relating to algorithms; it describes the method, while algorithm names the method itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「算法的」；它描述方法，而 algorithm 指方法本身。

entries.definition: By means of an algorithm; it modifies how something is done, not what it is.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「按算法地」；它修饰做事方式，不指事物本身。

entries.definition: A mathematical exponent word built from Greek logos and arithmos; the shared ending is coincidence of spelling, not shared origin.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊语 logos 与 arithmos 构成的数学指数词；相同词尾只是拼写巧合，并非同源。

entries.definition: Any agreed way of doing something; an algorithm is a procedure precise enough to be executed mechanically.
entries.definitionCN: 任何约定俗成的做法；algorithm 是精确到可机械执行的 procedure。

entries.definition: A way of working, often with judgment left to the user; an algorithm removes that judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 工作方式，常给使用者留出判断空间；algorithm 则取消这种判断。

entries.definition: A shortcut that usually works but has no guarantee; an algorithm promises a result for every allowed input.
entries.definitionCN: 通常有效但无保证的捷径；algorithm 则承诺对每个允许输入都给出结果。

entries.definition: The concrete code a machine runs; an algorithm is the method that the code implements, and one algorithm can be coded many ways.
entries.definitionCN: 机器运行的具体代码；algorithm 是代码所实现的方法，同一种算法可以有多种写法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real personal name, the real older spelling and the real computing phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的人名来源、真实的较早拼写与真实的计算机搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is a person: al-Khwarizmi taught the rules of calculation, and his Latinised name became the name of the rules.
normal.cn: 这个词来自一个人：花拉子米教计算规则，他的拉丁化名字就成了规则的名字。

normal.en: The older spelling algorism still means decimal calculation; algorithm is the respelled branch.
normal.cn: 较早拼写 algorism 仍指十进制计算；algorithm 是改拼后的分支。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the computing sense: sorting algorithm, search algorithm, encryption algorithm.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出计算机义：排序算法、搜索算法、加密算法。

normal.en: The -th- came from a mistaken link to Greek arithmos, number, and it stuck.
normal.cn: 词中的 -th- 来自与希腊语 arithmos「数」的错误联系，而且一直沿用下来。

normal.en: A logarithm looks like an algorithm but belongs to a different Greek family.
normal.cn: logarithm 看起来像 algorithm，却属于另一个希腊词族。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of doors, each opening only after the one before has closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊，每扇门都要前一扇关上后才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe that refuses to end until the pot is exactly full.
abstract.cn: 想象一份菜谱，锅没正好装满就绝不肯结束。

abstract.en: Picture a sorting hat that never asks for a second opinion.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶分院帽，从不征询第二个意见。

examples.en: The same algorithm can be written in five languages and still do the same work.
examples.cn: 同一个算法可以用五种语言写出，做的事仍然一样。

examples.en: A good algorithm says what to do when the input is empty.
examples.cn: 好的算法会说明输入为空时该怎么办。

examples.en: The team measured the algorithm's cost before adding more data.
examples.cn: 团队在增加数据之前先测了这套算法的开销。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱（al）哥（go）算（rith）法（m）」——爱算的哥们，一步步算到底

root: 九世纪数学家 al-Khwārizmī 之名 → 拉丁化 Algoritmi → 中世纪拉丁 algorismus → 英语 algorism；拼写受希腊语 arithmos「数」误类推而改为 algorithm。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one idea: a written method of calculation becomes any finite procedure, then a precise machine procedure, a formal object, a named routine, a decision rule, a product rule, a network rule and finally a recipe for life.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一个念头展开：一种写下来的计算方法，变成任何有限步骤，再变成精确的机器步骤、形式对象、具名例程、判定规则、产品规则、网络规则，最后变成生活里的套路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain of boxes joined by arrows, each step pointing to the next and ending in a single result.
core.cn: 核心意象：方框由箭头串起，每一步指向下一步，最后收在一个结果上。

branches.en: THE OLDEST LAYER: written rules for decimal arithmetic, preserved in the spelling algorism.
branches.cn: 最老的一层：书面的十进制运算规则，保存在拼写 algorism 里。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: steps that always end, and steps explicit enough for a machine to follow without guessing.
branches.cn: 步骤：总会终止的步骤，以及明确到机器无需猜测就能执行的步骤。

branches.en: OBJECT AND ROUTINE: the same procedure studied as a mathematical object and shipped as a named library routine.
branches.cn: 对象与例程：同一套步骤既作为数学对象被研究，又作为具名库例程被交付。

branches.en: DECIDING AND ROUTING: logic and networks both use mechanical rules to choose among possibilities.
branches.cn: 判定与路由：逻辑学与网络都用机械规则在多种可能中作选择。

branches.en: EVERYDAY RULE: a platform's ranking rule and a personal recipe are both the word at its broadest.
branches.cn: 日常规则：平台的排序规则与个人的做事套路，都是这个词最宽泛的用法。

intro.en: Algorithm is not built from Latin or Greek roots but from a Latinised Arabic personal name; later spellings and endings were added by English and by a mistaken Greek link.
intro.cn: algorithm 并非由拉丁或希腊词根构成，而是来自拉丁化的阿拉伯人名；后来的拼写与词尾是英语加上去的，另有一处希腊语误联。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin algorismus is the bridge form; the Greek arithmos that reshaped the spelling is a false association, not a real element.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 是中间的桥接形式；改写拼写的希腊语 arithmos 是错误联想，并非真实构件。

items.example: The article is frozen into the Latinised name.
items.exampleCN: 这个冠词被冻进了拉丁化的人名里。

items.example: The nisba identifies the scholar by his region.
items.exampleCN: 这个名字后缀用地名标识这位学者。

items.structure: Latinised form of the Arabic name
items.meaningCN: 这位学者名字的拉丁写法
items.example: Translators used the name for the method.
items.exampleCN: 译者用这个名字来指那套方法。

items.meaning: the decimal system and its rules
items.example: The Latin noun became English algorism.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词成了英语 algorism。

items.example: The Greek word pulled the spelling toward -th- by mistake.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词把拼写误拉向 -th-。

items.example: Algorism is the older doublet of algorithm.
items.exampleCN: algorism 是 algorithm 的较早同源异形词。

items.example: The respelling attached the word to number.
items.exampleCN: 这次改拼把词与「数」挂上了钩。

items.example: Algorithmic describes anything driven by such a procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmic 描述由这类步骤驱动的事物。

items.example: Algorithmically means by running the procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmically 意为「按算法执行」。

items.example: Algorithmics names the theory of procedures.
items.exampleCN: algorithmics 指关于步骤的理论。
